completion_decisions: Implement every paper-native problem, CHT, MOGOMEA variant and NSGA-II variant; exclude algorithms only cited as prior comparison context.
Treat Table-4 directions as meteorological wind-from and convert to flow-to.
Use binary MI normalized by ln(2), average-link UPGMA and stable index ties online; use geographic Euclidean distance with the same UPGMA rules offline.
Infer tau=0.5 from the published cluster-size equation and initial population/cluster values.
Use an unrestricted exact-deduplicated archive and the published FI threshold as the missing NIS base.
Use repair, resample and constraint domination respectively for the MOGOMEA, o-MOGOMEA and two NSGA-II multi-resolution roles.
Execute the full 192 fixed-resolution plus four multi-resolution role matrix with ten independent seeds and one million shared physical layout evaluations per run.
missing_information: author Python source and random states
MI normalization, UPGMA and cluster tie rules
archive capacity and exact duplicate behavior
numeric NIS base and hypervolume history implementation
machine-readable fronts, layouts, convergence arrays and timings

paper.authors: S. Rodrigues and P. Bauer and Peter A.N. Bosman
paper.title: Multi-Objective Optimization of Wind Farm Layouts—Complexity, Constraint Handling and Scalability

paper_linked_public_asset_candidates.use: primary paper identity and full text; no executable assets
institutional paper mirror; no executable assets

paper_source_conflicts: The article describes five CHTs but the case-study matrix uses four active CHTs at 2D/4D plus the naturally feasible 8D no-constraint construction; Figs. 13-15 repeat four CHT labels at all resolutions.
The paper specifies an NIS concept and hypervolume stopping conditions but does not publish a standalone numeric NIS base or exact history implementation.

scope.claim_boundary: academic flexible paper-equation reproduction of all twelve problems, four target algorithms, CHTs and multi-resolution roles; not author Python absent implementation choices random stream fronts trajectories or timings
